- **Delta:** $50,582M → $61,643M (+21.9% over 2 yrs); $58,048M → $61,643M (+6.2% YoY) [DOC-1]
- **United:** $44,955M → $57,063M (+26.9% over 2 yrs); $53,717M → $57,063M (+6.2% YoY) [DOC-1]
- **Southwest:** $23,814M → $27,483M (+15.4% over 2 yrs); $26,091M → $27,483M (+5.3% YoY) [DOC-1]
- **American:** $48,971M → $54,211M (+10.7% over 2 yrs); $52,788M → $54,211M (+2.7% YoY) [DOC-1]
- **Alaska:** $9,646M → $11,735M (+21.7% over 2 yrs); $10,426M → $11,735M (+12.6% YoY) [DOC-1]

**Important comparability note:** Alaska's FY2024 figures are **not directly comparable** to prior years or to peers on an organic basis. Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results (contributing **$869 million** in revenue) are consolidated only from that date forward [DOC-2]. This means a meaningful portion of Alaska's apparent YoY revenue acceleration (12.6%, the highest among the five) is attributable to inorganic growth from the acquisition rather than underlying demand or capacity trends. Excluding the ~$869M acquisition-related revenue, Alaska's standalone growth would be closer to $10,866M vs. $10,426M (~+4.2% YoY), below the organic growth rates of Delta and United.

**Excluding the Alaska/Hawaiian distortion**, United Airlines shows the strongest and most consistent revenue growth momentum: the highest 2-year growth rate (+26.9%) among all five carriers, and it is tied with Delta for the highest 1-year growth rate (+6.2%), both of which are organic (no major M&A activity disclosed for United or Delta in this period) [DOC-1].

ANSWER: United Airlines Holdings had the strongest revenue growth momentum on a comparable (organic) basis, with revenue growing +26.9% from FY2022 to FY2024 and +6.2% from FY2023 to FY2024 — the highest 2-year growth rate among the five carriers. Alaska Air Group posted a nominally higher 1-year growth rate (+12.6%), but this is not directly comparable because it includes $869 million in revenue from the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition completed on September 18, 2024, which inflates Alaska's apparent organic growth.
